new_entities.name: Pasireotide for Cushing's disease
aliases: somatostatin analog pasireotide for corticotroph adenoma
new_entities.description: Pasireotide treatment used to lower cortisol excess in pituitary-dependent Cushing's disease.

new_entities.name: Cortisol control
new_entities.description: Reduction or normalization of cortisol excess, usually measured with urinary free cortisol or related cortisol markers.

edges.effect_quant: Pasireotide produces meaningful cortisol lowering in a minority-to-moderate proportion of patients with Cushing's disease. A 2021 meta-analysis estimated disease control in 44% of 522 treated participants, the phase 3 registration trial showed a roughly 50% median urinary free cortisol reduction by month 2, and short-term phase 2 data showed urinary free cortisol fell in 76% of patients with normalization in 17%.
edges.population: adults with pituitary-dependent Cushing's disease, including de novo, persistent, or recurrent disease after surgery
edges.mechanism: Pasireotide binds somatostatin receptor subtype 5 on corticotroph adenomas, suppressing ACTH secretion and thereby lowering downstream cortisol production.
edges.summary: This is a clearly protective edge. Pasireotide is not universally effective and hyperglycemia is a major trade-off, but the cortisol-control signal is robust enough to make it a bona fide medical option for Cushing's disease.
edges.caveats: Normalization rates are far from universal, and some of the best response data come from uncontrolled studies. Hyperglycemia is a recurring adverse-effect constraint and should temper any impression that pasireotide is a simple win.

evidence.citation: Simoes Correa Galendi J et al 2021 Front Endocrinol (Lausanne)
evidence.notes: Effectiveness of Medical Treatment of Cushing's Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

effect_quant.comparator: pooled proportion of Cushing disease control with pasireotide across included studies

evidence.citation: Colao A et al 2012 N Engl J Med
evidence.notes: A 12-month phase 3 study of pasireotide in Cushing's disease.

effect_quant.comparator: participants meeting the primary month-6 urinary free cortisol endpoint without dose escalation

evidence.citation: Boscaro M et al 2009 J Clin Endocrinol Metab
evidence.notes: Treatment of pituitary-dependent Cushing's disease with the multireceptor ligand somatostatin analog pasireotide (SOM230): a multicenter, phase II trial.
